prompt.context_jp: 都心のオフィス街に、春の気配___まだ届いていなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 都心のオフィス街に、春の気配___まだ届いていなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the narrator's opening description.

feedback.correct_en: は frames 春の気配 as the topic being commented on, with an implicit contrast (spring hadn't arrived, though it's the season). This is the standard opening-line topic marker.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 春の気配 as brand-new information in a neutral existential statement, which clashes with the reflective, scene-setting tone.

prompt.context_jp: 冷たい風のなかで、そのスーパー派遣・大前春子の歩調___、驚くほど揺るがなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: そのスーパー派遣・大前春子の歩調___、驚くほど揺るがなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks Haruko's pace as the topic being described?

feedback.correct_en: 歩調は… sets Haruko's walking pace as the topic, then comments on it (unwavering). The narrator is characterizing her, not reporting a fresh event.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn this into a neutral event report, losing the characterizing nuance. を doesn't fit — 揺るがない is intransitive.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女の歩調は揺るがない。

prompt.context_jp: 幼いころから冷え性を患う彼女にとって、この朝の風___ことのほか身にこたえた。
prompt.prompt_jp: この朝の風___ことのほか身にこたえた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best captures 'this particular morning's wind' as a contrastive topic?

feedback.correct_en: は singles out この朝の風 contrastively — this particular morning's wind, as opposed to ordinary cold, hit her especially hard.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just announce a new subject with no contrastive flavor, flattening the point that today felt worse than usual.

contrast_examples.jp: 今日の風は特にきつい。

prompt.context_jp: そのなかで里中賢介主任だけ___、ほかの男たちとは違う色でその背中を眺めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 里中賢介主任だけ___、ほかの男たちとは違う色でその背中を眺めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits after 「だけ」, marking Satonaka in contrast to the other men?

feedback.correct_en: 〜だけは picks out Satonaka in explicit contrast to everyone else on the floor — the sentence then explains how he differs.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけが would present him as the exhaustive subject of a neutral event, without the contrastive 'as for him alone' nuance the narrator wants.

contrast_examples.en: He was the only one who came. (exhaustive listing)

prompt.context_jp: 湯呑みを持つ手の背には、長年の年季だけ___浮いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 湯呑みを持つ手の背には、長年の年季だけ___浮いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits — exhaustive 'nothing but years of experience showed'?

feedback.correct_en: だけが gives an exhaustive-listing reading: on the back of her hand, the ONLY thing visible was years of experience — nothing else.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would add contrastive 'as for only that', but the narrator is describing what literally shows on her hand, not contrasting it. を doesn't fit 浮く (intransitive).

prompt.context_jp: フロアの空気___、束の間、張りつめた。
prompt.prompt_jp: フロアの空気___、束の間、張りつめた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks a sudden new event — the air tensing up?

feedback.correct_en: が reports a fresh, momentary event: the air suddenly tensed when Haruko reached for the stapler. This is classic neutral-description が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'the floor's air' a topic being generally commented on, losing the sudden, event-like feel the narrator wants.

prompt.context_jp: 彼女の辞書に "不可能"と "残業"の文字___ない
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女の辞書に "不可能"と "残業"の文字___ない
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the narrator's set-phrase declaration about Haruko?

feedback.correct_en: 〜という文字はない is a fixed rhetorical pattern expressing contrastive emphasis — 'as for those words, they don't exist.' It implicitly contrasts with everything else that does.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be a neutral 'there isn't X' existential, missing the emphatic, almost declarative character of this famous line.

contrast_examples.jp: 私の辞書に不可能の文字はない。

prompt.context_jp: しかし彼___、その若さの分だけ、正社員としての段取りを選んだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: しかし彼___、その若さの分だけ、正社員としての段取りを選んだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits — Satonaka as the ongoing topic, contrasted with his inner hesitation?

feedback.correct_en: 彼は continues Satonaka as the topic from the previous sentence (he frowned, しかし彼は chose the salaryman path). しかし signals a contrast within the same topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce him as new information, but he's already the subject in the previous sentence — switching to が would feel disjointed.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は迷ったが、結局選んだ。
contrast_examples.en: He hesitated, but in the end chose. (continuing topic)

prompt.context_jp: ハンドルを握る指___、革を軋ませている。
prompt.prompt_jp: ハンドルを握る指___、革を軋ませている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best captures the vivid, descriptive detail?

feedback.correct_en: が is used for neutral-description sentences that paint a vivid scene — the fingers (as new focal detail) make the leather creak. Perfect for cinematic narration.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn the fingers into a known topic needing a comment, breaking the camera-pan feel.

prompt.context_jp: 助手席の派遣の横顔___、あくまで平坦だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 助手席の派遣の横顔___、あくまで平坦だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle treats Haruko's profile as the topic being commented on?

feedback.correct_en: は presents 横顔 as topic, then adjective-comments on it (was utterly flat). Also implicitly contrasts with Shoji's sweating in the previous line.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would announce the profile as new info, but it's a characterizing stative comment — は is natural.

prompt.context_jp: 小笠原の口ぶりには、あの派遣への嫉妬___すでに透けている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 小笠原の口ぶりには、あの派遣への嫉妬___すでに透けている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the jealousy as newly-revealed descriptive content?

feedback.correct_en: 嫉妬が透けている introduces the jealousy as a newly-noticed feature showing through his tone — neutral description with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would require 嫉妬 to be an established topic, but the narrator is pointing it out for the first time.

contrast_examples.en: His true feelings show through. (newly noticed)
He doesn't say his true feelings. (topic)

prompt.context_jp: 弁償の話___フロアに広がるのに、時間はかからなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 弁償の話___フロアに広がるのに、時間はかからなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'the compensation story' as the subject of a subordinate event?

feedback.correct_en: In subordinate clauses like 〜のに / 〜ので, the embedded subject typically takes が. 話が広がる reports the spreading as an event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside this subordinate clause would awkwardly make it a topic, which clashes with the main clause's own topic (時間はかからなかった).

prompt.context_jp: 春子___席に戻ると、フロアの空気は別種の張りを帯びていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 春子___席に戻ると、フロアの空気は別種の張りを帯びていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks Haruko inside the 〜と subordinate clause?

feedback.correct_en: The 〜と ('when') subordinate clause takes が for its subject. The main clause's topic (フロアの空気は) is separate.
feedback.incorrect_en: 春子は with と would wrongly promote her to the whole sentence's topic, when the real topic is the floor's atmosphere.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来ると、皆は黙った。
contrast_examples.en: When he came, everyone fell silent.

prompt.context_jp: 割れたサーバーの穴を埋めるように、男たちの声___高くなる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 男たちの声___高くなる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for this descriptive scene?

feedback.correct_en: が narrates the change-event: the men's voices rise. The sentence paints action, not a general comment about the voices.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 'the men's voices' into a topic needing a general characterization, losing the live-scene feel.

prompt.context_jp: 春子の帰る先を、森美雪___なぜかもう知っているような気がしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 森美雪___なぜかもう知っているような気がしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks Miyuki as the ongoing topic of the inner-feeling comment?

feedback.correct_en: 森美雪は establishes Miyuki as topic for the stative comment '〜気がしていた' (she had a feeling). Inner-state descriptions attached to a known character prefer は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn this into identification ('it was Miyuki who felt...'), which doesn't fit the quiet narrative close-up on her mind.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女はそんな気がしていた。
contrast_examples.en: She had that kind of feeling.
It was she who felt that way.

prompt.context_jp: 春子___、それをもう昨日のうちに見つけていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 春子___、それをもう昨日のうちに見つけていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits — Haruko as the main-clause topic?

feedback.correct_en: 春子は presents Haruko as topic and comments on what she had already done. The narrator is pulling back to show she was ahead of everyone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 春子が would answer 'who found it?' as new identification, but the sentence isn't identifying — it's commenting about Haruko who's already a known character.

contrast_examples.en: Haruko had already noticed. (comment on known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 派遣を口にする男たちに、この古株の女性社員___容赦がない。
prompt.prompt_jp: この古株の女性社員___容赦がない。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for the characterization of Asano?

feedback.correct_en: は sets Asano as the topic and gives a characterizing trait (shows no mercy). It's a general statement about her nature.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make this an identifying/new-info claim, awkward for a general description of someone's disposition.

prompt.context_jp: 「毛糸のパンツに "先輩"呼ばわり される___ ありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「毛糸のパンツに "先輩"呼ばわり される___ ありません」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill the blank with the expression Haruko uses to coldly refuse.

feedback.correct_en: 〜される筋合いはない means 'I have no reason/obligation to be ___-ed by you.' It's a sharp, dignified refusal — classic Haruko.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜わけにはいかない means 'can't bring myself to', and 〜つもりはない means 'don't intend to' — neither matches the 'you have no right to call me that' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: お前に説教される筋合いはない。
contrast_examples.en: You have no right to lecture me.

contrast_examples.jp: 説教するつもりはない。

prompt.context_jp: 「大前さん 目的のためなら 手段 ___ませんから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「大前さん 目的のためなら 手段 ___ませんから」
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb completes this famous set phrase about Haruko?

feedback.correct_en: 手段を選ばない is a fixed idiom meaning 'won't pick and choose means / will use any means necessary.' Satonaka is warning Shoji about her ruthlessness.
feedback.incorrect_en: 迷う and 考える are plausible verbs but don't form the idiom. 手段を迷わない / 考えない aren't natural fixed expressions.

contrast_examples.jp: 目的のためなら手段を選ばない。
contrast_examples.en: Will use any means for the goal.
To waver over which to pick.

prompt.context_jp: 「半年がかりで やっとの思いで 店長との___つくったのによ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「半年がかりで やっとの思いで 店長との___つくったのによ」
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes Shoji's business-world metaphor?

feedback.correct_en: パイプをつくる is business idiom for 'build a connection/pipeline' to a key person. Standard sales-world collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: ラインをつくる and ルートをつくる exist but don't fit this interpersonal-connection meaning. パイプ is the fixed collocation for 'contact/relationship.'

contrast_examples.jp: 役員とのパイプがある。
contrast_examples.en: Has a pipeline to the executives.

contrast_examples.jp: 販売ルートを開拓する。

prompt.context_jp: 「春子先輩って 正社員の人たちに 全然 ___使わないし」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「正社員の人たちに 全然 ___使わないし」
prompt.prompt_en: What word fits 「〜を使う」 meaning to flatter/suck up?

feedback.correct_en: おべっかを使う is a set phrase meaning 'to flatter / suck up.' Miyuki is admiring that Haruko never does this to permanent staff.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気配を使う and 気合を使う aren't natural collocations. 気を使う ('be considerate') would be a different meaning entirely.

contrast_examples.jp: 上司におべっかを使う。

prompt.context_jp: 「情報を守るのは 俺たち 正社員の仕事だ 派遣が そこまで ___なくていい」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「派遣が そこまで ___なくていい」
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb captures Shoji's dismissive 'temps shouldn't overstep'?

feedback.correct_en: 出しゃばる means 'to meddle / stick your nose where it doesn't belong.' It carries the exact condescending edge Shoji wants.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手伝う ('help') and 関わる ('be involved') are too neutral — they wouldn't convey Shoji's resentful push-back against Haruko's initiative.

contrast_examples.jp: 余計なことに出しゃばるな。
contrast_examples.en: Don't meddle where you don't belong.

prompt.context_jp: 一気にまくしたてる声には、同業者ゆえの苛立ちが濃く___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 同業者ゆえの苛立ちが濃く___。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'irritation seeping/showing through'?

feedback.correct_en: にじむ ('to seep/bleed through') collocates with emotions showing in voice/face — 感情がにじむ. Perfect for subtle irritation leaking out.
feedback.incorrect_en: 流れる is for liquids/tears flowing openly; 落ちる means 'drop/fall.' Neither captures the quiet bleeding-through of feeling.

prompt.context_jp: 「あんたは 断る___ないだけ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あんたは 断る___ないだけ」
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes Haruko's rebuke?

feedback.correct_en: 断る勇気がない — 'you simply lack the courage to say no.' Haruko is cutting through Miyuki's excuses.
feedback.incorrect_en: 権利がない ('no right') and 時間がない ('no time') don't match the moral/character critique Haruko is delivering.

prompt.context_jp: 「壊れちゃったんじゃなくて ___んでしょ？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「壊れちゃったんじゃなくて ___んでしょ？」
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb form captures Asano's accusation (not 'it broke' but 'you broke it')?

feedback.correct_en: 壊す (transitive) blames the agent — 'YOU broke it.' Asano is pointedly correcting Miyuki's intransitive excuse.
feedback.incorrect_en: 壊れる (intransitive) is what Miyuki said to deflect; 壊される (passive) would mean 'it got broken (by someone else).' Neither pins the blame on Miyuki.

prompt.context_jp: Haruko sharply shuts down Satonaka's flamenco talk at work.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most like Haruko's cool, formal workplace refusal?

choices.text: 朝から 意味の分からない話題を 私に振らないでください
朝から わけわからない話 ふらないでよ
朝から そんな話するの やめてほしいんだけど

feedback.correct_en: Option A keeps the stiff, polished '〜ないでください' and the formal vocabulary (話題を振る) that defines Haruko's professional voice. It's exactly how she speaks on-the-clock.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is too casual (〜ないでよ) and C is middle-ground conversational — both would soften Haruko's trademark coldness toward coworkers.

prompt.context_jp: Haruko turning down Shoji's request to accompany him on sales.
prompt.prompt_en: Which refusal sounds most natural in Haruko's register?

choices.text: 販売二課の仕事は 私には関わりございません
販売二課の仕事は 私と関係ありません
販売二課の仕事は 私は知りません

feedback.correct_en: 関わりございません uses the humble/stiff ございます form, perfect for Haruko's icy-polite tone when brushing off an unwanted request.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is grammatically fine but flat; C ('I don't know anything about it') shifts the meaning to ignorance rather than scope-of-contract refusal.

contrast_examples.jp: 私には関わりございません。
contrast_examples.en: It has no bearing on me. (formal distance)

prompt.context_jp: Haruko leaves promptly at lunchtime, declining further conversation.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line fits Haruko's clipped, business-like exit?

choices.text: 定食屋が混みますので失礼します
定食屋 混んじゃうから もう行くね
定食屋が混むから 失礼

feedback.correct_en: 〜ますので失礼します is the standard polite workplace exit formula. The 〜ますので reasoning + 失礼します closing is exactly Haruko's tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is casual girltalk; C mixes polite 混む with blunt 失礼 — inconsistent register that doesn't match her careful professionalism.

contrast_examples.jp: 用事がありますので失礼します。
contrast_examples.en: I have an errand, so excuse me. (polite exit)
Got stuff to do, heading out. (casual)

prompt.context_jp: Haruko telling Miyuki, in a rare blunt moment, to leave her alone.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing captures Haruko's sharp, exact command?

choices.text: あと30秒 話しかけないで
あと30秒ぐらい 話しかけないでください
もうちょっと 話しかけないで

feedback.correct_en: The precise '30秒' with no softeners is signature Haruko — crisp, numeric, bluntly plain-form. She measures everything.
feedback.incorrect_en: B adds polite ください (too soft for this moment); C swaps the exact figure for a vague もうちょっと, losing her calculated precision.

prompt.context_jp: Haruko refusing a coffee-run errand that's not in her contract.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds like Haruko's by-the-book refusal?

choices.text: 私の契約には その業務は入っておりません
私の契約に その仕事は入ってないんです
それ 契約外の仕事なんで ちょっと…

feedback.correct_en: 業務 (not 仕事) and 入っておりません (humble おります) give the exact bureaucratic armor Haruko uses to deflect — strictly contract-language.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses casual 仕事 and plainer 入ってない; C trails off with ちょっと, which is apologetic softening. Haruko never softens.

contrast_examples.jp: 契約には含まれておりません。
contrast_examples.en: It isn't included in the contract. (formal)

contrast_examples.jp: 契約に入ってないんで…
contrast_examples.en: It's not in my contract, so… (soft refusal)
